question: Is the issue #588 competitor-mechanic assimilation study runnable today, with MEC-DARWINIAN_WORKFLOW_EVOLUTION as the designated comparator?
the_important_finding: The repository has already reached this verdict and recorded it honestly. research/paper6_scoped_utility_v1/PREREGISTRATION_V1.json carries arm E_LLM_JUDGE_FITNESS, source_mechanic MEC-DARWINIAN_WORKFLOW_EVOLUTION, with kind BLOCKED and state CANNOT_CHECK, declining to run it because 'A simulated judge with an assumed error model would be a sensitivity model, not a measurement.' That refusal is pinned by tests/test_paper6_scoped_utility_v1.py::test_llm_judge_arm_is_blocked_and_not_simulated. No new decision is needed; the existing one is correct and should not be reopened by substituting a simulated judge.

designated_comparator.transfer_obligation_verbatim: Faithful-transfer challenger: workflow-level mutation with an LLM-judge fitness, run to see whether it gains or gates-fails. Repaired challenger: same mutation operator with the fitness replaced by a RAKL evidence gate. The contrast between the two is the actual experiment.
designated_comparator.rakl_analogue_verbatim: Self-RAKL mechanic evolution. This is the closest external system to ORION's own recursive layer and therefore the most informative comparator in the registry.
designated_comparator.anchor_verification_status: NOT_VERIFIED — arXiv:2603.28986 appears in no row of the Confirmed table in research/external_research_agents/ANCHOR_VERIFICATION.md; Mimosa is named there only in Correction 2 as a class-D system the issue had missed
designated_comparator.version_freeze: CANNOT_CHECK on all four fields (evaluated_version, evaluated_date, commit, license)

registry_health_bearing_on_this.taxonomy_note_verbatim: no public class-D suite exists — ORION's self-improvement claims cannot be externally validated by any Tier 1 suite currently in the registry

cheapest_unblocking_move: The internal faithful-versus-repaired contrast does not require Mimosa and does not require the UNDETERMINED comparator class to be resolved. It requires exactly two things that do not exist: a workflow-level mutation operator over editable RAKL workflows, and an LLM-judge budget. The mutation operator is the harder and more valuable of the two, because it is a prerequisite for any future Self-RAKL mechanic-evolution experiment regardless of comparator. Building it is the highest-leverage next step; simulating the judge is explicitly not.
